{"timeline":[{"headline":"Foundation of Zurich","text":"Zurich was founded by the Romans in 15 BCE as a tax-collecting point called 'Turicum'.","date":"-0015"},{"headline":"First Mention of Zurich","text":"The first mention of the city as 'Zurich' dates back to 929 AD.","date":"0929"},{"headline":"Charter of Zurich","text":"In 1218, Zurich was granted the status of a free imperial city by Emperor Frederick II.","date":"1218"},{"headline":"Zurich Joins the Swiss Confederation","text":"Zurich joined the Swiss Confederation in 1351, becoming one of its member states.","date":"1351"},{"headline":"Reformation in Zurich","text":"In 1519, Huldrych Zwingli began the Protestant Reformation in Zurich, leading to significant religious and social changes.","date":"1519"},{"headline":"Zurich's First Railway","text":"The first railway in Zurich was opened in 1847, connecting Zurich with Baden.","date":"1847"},{"headline":"Establishment of ETH Zurich","text":"The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH Zurich) was established in 1855, becoming a leading university in science and technology.","date":"1855"},{"headline":"Opening of Zurich Airport","text":"Zurich Airport was officially opened in 1948, becoming the largest and busiest airport in Switzerland.","date":"1948"},{"headline":"Zurich's Population Growth","text":"As of January 2023, the municipality of Zurich had 443,037 inhabitants, reflecting its growth as a major urban center.","date":"2023-01"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Founding of Fairfax County","text":"Fairfax County was officially formed in 1742 from the northern part of Prince William County. It was named after Thomas Fairfax, 6th Lord Fairfax of Cameron, who owned the land.","date":"1742"},{"headline":"Fairfax County Courthouse Built","text":"The Fairfax County Courthouse was constructed in 1800, serving as a central location for county government and judicial activities.","date":"1800"},{"headline":"Civil War Impact","text":"During the American Civil War (1861-1865), Fairfax County was a significant location due to its proximity to Washington, D.C. It saw numerous troop movements and skirmishes.","date":"1861"},{"headline":"Post-War Growth","text":"Following World War II, Fairfax County experienced significant suburban growth, driven by its proximity to Washington, D.C., and the expansion of federal government jobs.","date":"1945"},{"headline":"Establishment of Dulles International Airport","text":"Dulles International Airport, located in Fairfax County, was opened in 1962, significantly impacting the county's development and economy.","date":"1962"},{"headline":"Metro Expansion","text":"The Washington Metro system expanded into Fairfax County in the 1980s, improving transportation and contributing to further suburban growth.","date":"1980"},{"headline":"Population Milestone","text":"By the 2020 census, Fairfax County's population reached 1,150,309, making it the most populous county in Virginia and the Washington metropolitan area.","date":"2020"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Formation of the Bulgaria National Football Team","text":"The Bulgaria national football team was formed in 1922, representing Bulgaria in men's international football.","date":"1922"},{"headline":"First International Match","text":"Bulgaria played its first official international match against Austria on May 21, 1924, in Vienna, Austria.","date":"1924-05-21"},{"headline":"First World Cup Appearance","text":"Bulgaria made its first appearance in the FIFA World Cup in 1962, held in Chile.","date":"1962"},{"headline":"First European Championship Appearance","text":"Bulgaria qualified for its first UEFA European Championship in 1968, held in Italy.","date":"1968"},{"headline":"Historic World Cup Performance","text":"Bulgaria reached the semi-finals of the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, achieving their best-ever performance by finishing fourth.","date":"1994"},{"headline":"First European Championship Win","text":"Bulgaria achieved its first win in a European Championship match during the UEFA Euro 1996, defeating Romania 1-0 on June 13, 1996.","date":"1996-06-13"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"First Recorded Outbreak of Ergotism","text":"The first recorded outbreak of ergotism occurred in the Rhine Valley in the year 857. This event marked the beginning of documented cases of ergot poisoning, which was later known as Saint Anthony's fire due to the burning sensations experienced by sufferers.","date":"0857"},{"headline":"Ergotism in the Middle Ages","text":"Throughout the Middle Ages, ergotism was a common affliction in Europe, particularly affecting those who consumed rye bread contaminated with the Claviceps purpurea fungus. The disease was characterized by severe symptoms, including hallucinations, gangrene, and convulsions.","date":"1000"},{"headline":"Saint Anthony's Fire Epidemics","text":"During the 10th to 13th centuries, several epidemics of ergotism, known as Saint Anthony's fire, were recorded across Europe. Monasteries dedicated to Saint Anthony became centers for treating those afflicted by the disease.","date":"1000"},{"headline":"Discovery of Ergot's Medicinal Uses","text":"In the 16th century, ergot was discovered to have medicinal properties and was used to induce labor and control bleeding after childbirth. This marked the beginning of its use in medicine, despite its toxic potential.","date":"1500"},{"headline":"Identification of Ergot Alkaloids","text":"In the 19th century, scientists began to isolate and identify the alkaloids present in ergot, which were responsible for its toxic and medicinal effects. This led to a better understanding of ergotism and its causes.","date":"1800"},{"headline":"Synthesis of LSD from Ergot Alkaloids","text":"In 1938, Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann synthesized LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide) from ergot alkaloids. This discovery highlighted the psychoactive properties of ergot derivatives and their potential for both therapeutic and recreational use.","date":"1938"},{"headline":"Ergotism in Modern Times","text":"With improved agricultural practices and food safety regulations, ergotism has become rare in modern times. However, it remains a concern in areas where ergot-contaminated grains are consumed.","date":"2000"}]}
